name: What Really Grinds My Gears
aka: You Know What Really Grinds My Gears
look: A Family Guy frame inside a gray TV screen border. Peter Griffin, in a dark suit and red tie, sits at a news desk with papers, mouth open mid-rant. Behind him on a purple wall hangs a yellow graphic with blue gears reading "What Really Grinds My Gears".
use: A rant about a petty annoyance. The caption names the thing that irritates you, usually framed as "You know what really grinds my gears?" followed by a specific pet peeve, like people who walk slowly in groups.
slots: the setup, usually "You know what really grinds my gears?" (top)
examples: You know what really grinds my gears?
People who reply "k" to a long message
You know what really grinds my gears?
Phone chargers that only work at one specific angle
describe: family guy peter as a news anchor ranting at a desk
cartoon dad newscaster with a gears sign behind him
cartoon man at a news desk complaining about a pet peeve
tv segment sign says what really grinds my gears
fat cartoon guy in suit and red tie yelling on the news
origin: Peter Griffin's recurring "What Really Grinds My Gears" news segment from Family Guy.
